title: 5.5.9 Lab: Give the class its own isAlive()
description: The scene asks `hp > 0` twice, by hand. Write `isAlive()` on the class and ask it instead, so the question 'is this enemy still up?' has exactly one answer in one place. What you see on screen does not change.

steps.title: Write isAlive()
steps.instructions: Add an `isAlive()` method to the class. It takes no arguments and returns `true` while `this.hp` is above 0, `false` once it is not.
hints: It is a one-line method: `return` followed by a comparison on `this.hp`.
5.5.6 (Worked Example: The number anyone can set) has the same method written out.

steps.title: Ask the class, not the number
steps.instructions: In `draw()`, replace both `e.hp > 0` checks with `e.isAlive()`. Run it and press Space six times: nothing about what you see should change. That is the point — the rule has moved, not the behaviour.
hints: There are two of them: the one inside the `text(...)` line and the one on the next line that sets the colour.

requirements.title: isAlive() returns whether this.hp is above 0
requirements.description: The class has an `isAlive()` method that returns a comparison on `this.hp`. Help: 5.5.6 (Worked Example: The number anyone can set)

requirements.title: draw() asks isAlive() instead of comparing hp
requirements.description: The scene calls `e.isAlive()` rather than comparing `e.hp` itself. Help: 5.5.6 (Worked Example: The number anyone can set)
